## feature

## fix

### Consensus MAPQ overstated mapping confidence in repeats

```
level: high
```

#### reason

The consensus record took its MAPQ from the ORIGINAL aligner values, so a
repeat-ambiguous pair whose adjusted mates carry MAPQ 3 merged into a
MAPQ-60 record. This violates the spec's core guarantee: never falsely
assign 60 to exact matches in repeats.

#### description

```
type: text
```

1. `try_merge` gained a `merged_mapq` parameter separating the output MAPQ
   from the eligibility MAPQ on the structs.
2. `_both_mapped` computes `merged_mapq = min(adjusted R1, adjusted R2)`
   before restoring the original MAPQs onto the structs.
3. Eligibility (`--min-mapq`) still gates on the original aligner MAPQ, per
   the documented policy; only the output value changed.

#### before

Merged `pair_repeat` (tandem repeat, placement ambiguous) carried MAPQ 60
while both adjusted mates carried 3. The committed
`data/synthetic/expected_merged.bam` encoded the bug.

#### after

The consensus carries min(adjusted) = 3; unique unchanged pairs still
merge at 60. Regenerated expected outputs and README now state the policy.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
Reproduction before the fix, then after (same script):

```
before: merged pair_repeat flag=0 pos=400 mapq=60 cigar=16M
after:  merged pair_repeat flag=0 pos=400 mapq=3  cigar=16M
```

Regenerated committed output (`samtools view data/synthetic/expected_merged.bam`):

```
pair_repeat  0  chr1  401  3  16M  ...  MD:Z:16  NM:i:0
```

Regression: `tests/test_merge.py::TestMergedMapqPolicy` (2 tests).
Suite: 130 passed.
:::

### Pair-evaluation truncation could imply false uniqueness

```
level: high
```

#### reason

Exhausting `--max-pair-evaluations` broke the search loops without setting
`PairChoice.truncated`, so the MAPQ policy saw an untruncated, unambiguous
search and assigned 60 at placements whose equivalents were never explored
— the exact false-confidence class the policy exists to prevent.

#### description

```
type: text
```

1. `select_pair` now computes `search_truncated = evaluated >=
   cfg.max_pair_evaluations` and ORs it into `PairChoice.truncated`.
2. Ending exactly at the cap also counts as truncated (conservative
   direction).
3. The existing `min(orig, 10)` rule then applies through the unchanged
   `adjusted_mapq` policy.

#### before

`--max-pair-evaluations 1 --max-candidates-per-read 100` on the repeat
pair yielded MAPQ 60/60 at an ambiguous placement (default budget: 3/3).

#### after

The same invocation yields MAPQ 10/10 (`min(orig, 10)`), never 60.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
```
default: pair_repeat pos=400 mapq=3
capped:  pair_repeat pos=400 mapq=10   <-- after fix (was 60)
```

Regressions: `tests/test_pairing.py::TestSelectPair::test_eval_budget_truncation_flags_choice`,
`test_discovery_truncation_propagates`;
`tests/test_candidates_mapq.py::TestAmbiguousRepeatPair::test_capped_pair_search_caps_mapq`.
:::

### Disagreement finalize loaded every spilled row into memory

```
level: high
```

#### reason

`_spill_stream` materialized each spill file as a Python list and
`finalize` held one list per spill, so peak memory grew with the entire
dataset (~145 bytes/row) — defeating the documented
`--max-aggregation-records` bound and risking OOM on large inputs. Plain
generators alone were insufficient: `heapq.merge` pulls one batch per
spill, so many small spills would still scale with spill count.

#### description

```
type: text
```

1. `_spill_stream` is a generator over `iter_batches` (one Parquet batch
   resident per open stream).
2. New `_reduce_spills` cascades merges until at most `_MERGE_FANIN = 16`
   spill files remain, writing intermediates through a batched
   `_write_spill_rows` (streaming writer; intermediates stay
   uncompressed as before).
3. Finalize memory is now a function of configuration (fan-in × batch
   size) plus the in-memory buffer — never of dataset size.

#### before

60,000 positions with a 1000-entry threshold: finalize peaked at 8.7 MB,
scaling linearly with total rows.

#### after

Same workload: 2.2 MB peak. 100,000-position regression asserts peak
< 10 MB where the eager path measured ~15 MB.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
```
spills=59 positions=60000
before: finalize peak=8.7 MB (max_aggregation_records=1000)
after:  finalize peak=2.2 MB
```

Regressions: `tests/test_integration.py::TestBoundedMemory::test_spill_finalize_memory_stays_bounded`
(tracemalloc bound + generator contract); existing spill-correctness tests
(`test_spilling_aggregator_matches_direct_result`,
`test_aggregator_unit_spill_merge`) still pass.
:::

### Contained mates produced the wrong trailing soft clip

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

The trailing-clip owner was the mate with the later START. A contained
mate starts later but ends earlier, so its internal clip was promoted to
the fragment's outer edge while the container's outer clip was dropped —
a spec §8 violation (outer soft clips preserved) that also corrupted the
merged sequence. Medium: wrong sequence content, but limited to contained
mates with clips.

#### description

```
type: text
```

The trail-clip owner is now the mate with the largest aligned `end0`
(`trail = struct1 if struct1.end0 >= struct2.end0 else struct2`); the lead
owner stays the smallest `start0`. In a contained pair one read correctly
owns both outer clips.

#### before

`40M3S` at 500 containing `10M2S` at 510 merged to `40M2S`, appending the
contained mate's 2 internal clip bases.

#### after

The same pair merges to `40M3S` with the container's 3 outer clip bases.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
```
before: merged contained pos=500 cigar=40M2S
after:  merged contained pos=500 cigar=40M3S
        query_sequence == ref[500:540] + "NNN"
```

Regression: `tests/test_merge.py::TestOuterSoftClips::test_container_owns_trailing_outer_clip`.
:::

### Orphan adjustment left stale mate coordinates

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

`_adjust_single` moved the unmapped mate's POS to the mapped mate's new
locus but never refreshed its RNEXT/PNEXT, which kept pointing at the
pre-adjustment position — inconsistent metadata for every downstream tool
that reads mate fields. Medium: metadata-only corruption, placements and
sequences were already correct.

#### description

```
type: text
```

Two lines in `_adjust_single` now set the unmapped mate's
`next_reference_id/start` to the mapped record's post-adjustment
coordinates (SAM spec: an unmapped read's mate fields reference the mapped
mate).

#### before

After the mapped mate slid 416 → 400: unmapped mate POS 400 but
`rnext=0:416`.

#### after

Both records' RNEXT/PNEXT point at 400.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
```
out: orphan flag=65  pos=400 mapq=3  cigar=16M  rnext=0:400
out: orphan flag=133 pos=400 mapq=0  cigar=None rnext=0:400  <-- was 0:416
```

Regression: `tests/test_classify_policy.py::TestRecordPolicy::test_unmapped_mate_rnext_follows_movement`.
:::

### Index outputs bypassed overwrite and collision validation

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

Derived `.bai` destinations were absent from `validate_paths`, so an
existing index was silently overwritten without `--force` (violating the
fail-loud spec §9), and an index path equal to another declared output
would clobber that output at publish time. Medium: requires `--index-output`
and specific pre-existing files, but the collision case destroys an output.

#### description

```
type: text
```

With `--index-output`, `validate_paths` now folds each derived
`<bam>.bai` path into the output set under the role `index for <role>`;
the existing distinctness and existence-requires-`--force` checks then
cover them, mirroring exactly how the pipeline derives the destinations.

#### before

A stale `adj.bam.bai` was silently replaced (exit 0) without `--force`.

#### after

Exit 2 with `index for adjusted_bam output already exists ... Use --force
to overwrite.`; collision cases (`--unmerged-bam m.bam.bai` under
`--merged-bam m.bam`) are rejected before processing starts.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
```
second run (no --force; only a stale .bai exists) exit=2
pairmerge: error: index for adjusted_bam output already exists:
           /tmp/.../adj.bam.bai. Use --force to overwrite.
```

Regressions: `tests/test_cli.py::TestPathValidation::test_existing_index_without_force_refused`,
`test_index_colliding_with_output_rejected`.
:::

## limitation

### Finalize memory is bounded by configuration, not zero

```
level: low
```

#### reason

Low: the bound is real and configuration-controlled; only its magnitude
is the limitation.

#### description

```
type: text
```

Spill finalize still holds fan-in (16) × one Parquet batch of rows plus
the in-memory buffer. With default settings that is roughly one million
rows of headroom — two configurable constants, independent of dataset
size, but not a hard small cap.

#### evidence

```
level: medium
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
Measured 2.2 MB peak at 60k positions with a 1000-entry threshold
(`/tmp` reproduction, tracemalloc); bound asserted in
`tests/test_integration.py::TestBoundedMemory::test_spill_finalize_memory_stays_bounded`.
:::

## caveat

### Intentional behavior changes for existing users

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

Medium: three user-visible behavior changes ship with this batch; users
must know before upgrading.

#### description

```
type: text
```

1. Merged consensus records of repeat-ambiguous pairs now carry the
   conservative MAPQ (3 instead of 60 in the synthetic example); pipelines
   filtering merged BAMs by MAPQ ≥ 30 will see fewer repeat reads pass.
2. Runs that previously succeeded by silently overwriting stale `.bai`
   files now exit 2; they need `--force` like every other output.
3. `--max-pair-evaluations`-limited runs now cap MAPQ at 10 instead of
   granting 60.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
All three changes are pinned by new regression tests (see the fix items);
EXPECTED.md and the README MAPQ/merging sections state the new behavior.
:::

## assumption

### tracemalloc measures the dominant allocation path

```
level: low
```

#### reason

Low: a test-infrastructure assumption, stated so a future flake can be
diagnosed quickly.

#### description

```
type: text
```

The finalize memory regression asserts a tracemalloc peak, which tracks
Python-side allocations (the row tuples and strings that dominated the
eager path) but not native Arrow buffers. The 10 MB bound carries enough
margin for machine variance; native-side regression is not covered.

#### evidence

```
level: unknown
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
None
:::

## conclusion

### All six verified review findings are fixed and regression-pinned

```
level: high
```

#### reason

High: this is the batch's outcome statement, backed by the full gate run.

#### description

```
type: text
```

1. All six fixes landed as one batch, each with a dedicated regression
   test (10 new tests total); the suite grew from 120 to 130 passing.
2. The evaluation turn's reproduction script, re-run unchanged, confirms
   every fixed behavior at the exact call sites that demonstrated the bugs.
3. Lint, format, `samtools quickcheck`, and the benchmark show no
   regressions; committed synthetic expected outputs were regenerated to
   encode the corrected MAPQ policy.
4. The extra dead-code finding (`single_read_ambiguity`) was removed.
